Sam: Quick follow-up from today’s all-hands — can you clarify how our mission to make high‑performance inference accessible actually guides product tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private?
Kate (CEO): Short answer: prioritize predictable economics + low friction. Hosted for fast iteration, Dedicated when customers need throughput guarantees, Private when isolation/compliance is the blocker.
Sam: Got it — any hard rules? when do we steer customers away from Hosted? :thinking:
Kate (CEO): We steer when one of three is true: 1) data residency/SOC requirements, 2) steady high qps where reserved pricing is cheaper, 3) latency SLOs that need colocated infra. Not a hard blacklist, more a cost/operational signal.
Maria: How should PMs prioritize features against that mission? e.g., cheaper batching vs more model variants for compatibility?
Devon: From infra POV, batching/configs often yield larger unit-cost reductions for long‑tail customers. Model variants help coverage but add ops complexity.
Kate (CEO): PM rule of thumb: if the change reduces per‑token cost or improves tail latency without adding much operational burden, it ranks high. If it's one-off model coverage for niche architectures, deprioritize unless tied to a high-value customer.
Kevin: On competitors — how do we talk about our edge without sounding like "we're just faster"? Sales keeps hearing pushback: "all clouds scale GPUs"
Jasmeet: Echoing Kevin. Need crisp positioning vs managed endpoints (easy) and self-hosted runtimes (control).
Kate (CEO): Messaging: we win on predictable economics + operational primitives. Two quick pillars to lean on in GTM: 1) Serving primitives (autoscale, canary rollouts, fallback variants) that reduce engineering toil; 2) Transparent unit economics + suggestions (Optimize tooling) that cut customer bills. Not just raw latency.
Kevin: Any quantitative claims allowed? e.g., "up to 3x lower cost" — legal will freak unless vetted.
Kate (CEO): Use qualitative claims + customer stories until legal signoff. Example: "customers reduced inference cost significantly using Optimize's batching + caching". For hard numbers, route through GTM ops and legal.
Maria: Follow-up operational question — if a customer starts on Hosted and grows fast, what's the migration path to Dedicated? downtime?
Devon: Typical: export model pins and configs, we provide a migration window with canary traffic to Dedicated. Expect minimal downtime if KV cache warmup is accepted; we support warm start procedures.
Sam: Nice. Last one — how should ICs summarize this in 2‑3 lines for slack/office docs?
Kate (CEO): "We focus on production economics: make inference predictable, cost‑efficient, and reliable. Hosted gets you started fast; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost; Private provides isolation for regulated workloads." :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Meeting recording uploaded — https://redwood.internal/rec/1725500000
Jasmeet: Thanks — moving this to #product-playbooks as a short note.
Sam: Perfect, thanks everyone.
